fidelity: All 12 frozen F-AHL10 cases pass the preregistered Richards fidelity and nonlinear-path gates before timing interpretation.
finding: The selected derivative-consistent adaptive hydraulic representation is faster than analytical hydraulics in every tested material/regime case, with a median complete-Richards CPU reduction of about 15.1% across the 12-case matrix.
scientific_interpretation: The speed benefit is not obtained by independently tabulating theta, C and K.
Preserving the theta-C derivative relationship is required to preserve the nonlinear solution path in the tested cases.
K requires materially tighter error control than the initial 1e-2 screen for wet/dry endpoint fidelity; 3e-4 is the loosest prospectively tested tolerance that passes the frozen 12-case matrix.

The extreme O05 dry tail should not consume adaptive support below the previously reconciled negligible-storage relevance scale; outside the represented domain the authoritative analytical provider remains active.
next_action: Broaden qualification beyond four unimodal materials and prescribed-head lower-boundary cases, then decide whether a production-oriented implementation/admission work unit is justified.
nonclaims: This is not yet a whole-SWAP or MultiSWAP speedup claim.
The result does not cover all SWAP hydraulic model families or lower-boundary modes.
